references.text: God tells Moses that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same theme as in 7:3
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, fulfilling the promise in 7:3
God hardens Pharaoh's heart to display His signs and wonders in Egypt
God's signs and wonders in Egypt, as foretold in 7:3
Moses recalls the signs and wonders God performed in Egypt
The Lord performed signs and wonders against Egypt and Pharaoh
Reference to the great signs and wonders in Egypt
God's signs in Egypt and wonders on the fields of Zoan
They performed His signs among them, wonders in the land of Ham
He sent signs and wonders against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants
Paul quotes God's hardening of Pharaoh to demonstrate His power
Warning against hardening the heart, an allusion to Pharaoh's hardened heart
Expands the motif from Pharaoh's individual stubbornness to a collective action against the entire Egyptian army to achieve God's glorification.
Connects God's purpose with hardness directly to the concrete event where Pharaoh pursues the Israelites, completing the signs mentioned in 7:3.
Creates a theological arc from God's plan to perform signs (7:3) to the final deliverance that follows these signs (3:20).
Completes the theological circle: Hardness -> signs/miracles -> God's glorification -> recognition of the Lord.
Confirms the causal connection: Hardness is a prerequisite for performing the signs mentioned in 7:3.
